```{r}
#| include: false
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,

```

GEPA improves a module's instructions through *reflection*: it scores candidate
instructions, shows a reflection model the rows a candidate got wrong along
with your metric's textual feedback, and asks it to rewrite the instructions.
Over several generations, the strongest candidates survive and evolve.

> **Note on the offline runner:** To execute end-to-end during documentation
> builds without API keys, this walkthrough uses a deterministic stand-in
> `task_chat` and `reflection_chat` (defined in a hidden setup chunk). It
> illustrates the real GEPA loop, lineage, and budget accounting; on your own
> data, swap in live ellmer Chats as shown at the end of the page.

## 1. Define the task and keep three splits separate

Suppose you want to route customer support tickets as `urgent` (current service
outage or compromised account) or `routine` (everything else). Keep three
datasets strictly separate:

- **`train`**: where GEPA collects failures and feedback for reflection.
- **`validation`**: where GEPA scores candidates and picks parents.
- **`holdout`**: touched only once, at the very end, to verify whether the
  winning instructions actually generalize.

```{r task-data}
#| message: false
library(dsprrr)

train <- data.frame(
  ticket = c(
    "Checkout is unavailable for every customer during an outage.",
    "Please update the billing contact.",
    "An unknown user took over my account.",
    "When is the next invoice due?"
  ),
  severity = c("urgent", "routine", "urgent", "routine")
)

validation <- data.frame(
  ticket = c(
    "A production outage is blocking every customer.",
    "A stranger gained access to my account.",
    "Can I change my billing email?"
  ),
  severity = c("urgent", "urgent", "routine")
)

holdout <- data.frame(
  ticket = c(
    "A service outage is stopping password resets.",
    "An attacker accessed my account overnight.",
    "Please add a second billing contact.",
    "Where can I see next month's invoice?"
  ),
  severity = c("urgent", "urgent", "routine", "routine")
)

program <- module(signature(
  "ticket -> severity: enum('urgent', 'routine')",
  instructions = "Use a quick baseline rule."
))
```

```{r offline-fixture}
#| include: false
fixture_chat_class <- R6::R6Class(
  "Chat",
  public = list(
    turns = NULL,
    initialize = function(model, responder) {
      self$turns <- list()
      private$model <- ellmer::Model(name = model, extra_args = list())
      private$provider <- ellmer::Provider(name = "fixture", base_url = "")
      private$responder <- responder
    },
    chat = function(prompt, ...) {
      private$responder(paste(as.character(prompt), collapse = "\n"), NULL, ...)
    },
    chat_structured = function(prompt, type, ...) {
      private$responder(paste(as.character(prompt), collapse = "\n"), type, ...)
    },
    stream = function(...) character(),
    get_turns = function() self$turns,
    set_turns = function(turns) {
      self$turns <- turns
      invisible(self)
    },
    last_turn = function(role = NULL) NULL,
    get_model = function() private$model@name,
    get_provider = function() private$provider,
    get_model_object = function() private$model
  ),
  private = list(model = NULL, provider = NULL, responder = NULL),
  lock_objects = FALSE,
  parent_env = globalenv()
)

new_fixture_chat <- function(model, responder) {
  audit <- new.env(parent = emptyenv())
  audit$prompts <- character()
  wrapped_responder <- function(prompt, type, ...) {
    prompt <- paste(as.character(prompt), collapse = "\n")
    audit$prompts <- c(audit$prompts, prompt)
    responder(prompt, type, ...)
  }
  list(
    chat = fixture_chat_class$new(model, wrapped_responder),
    audit = audit
  )
}

partial_rule <- paste(
  "Mark a ticket urgent when it reports an explicit outage;",
  "otherwise mark it routine."
)
complete_rule <- paste(
  "Mark tickets urgent when they report a current service outage",
  "or compromised account; otherwise mark them routine."
)

task_fixture <- new_fixture_chat("fixture-task", function(prompt, type, ...) {
  prompt_lines <- strsplit(prompt, "\n", fixed = TRUE)[[1L]]
  input_header <- grep("^# Input:", prompt_lines)
  ticket_line <- grep("^ticket: ", prompt_lines, value = TRUE)
  if (length(input_header) != 1L || length(ticket_line) != 1L) {
    stop("Task fixture could not read one ticket from the prompt")
  }

  instructions <- paste(
    prompt_lines[seq_len(input_header - 1L)],
    collapse = "\n"
  )
  ticket <- sub("^ticket: ", "", ticket_line[[1L]])
  outage_rule <- grepl("explicit outage", instructions, fixed = TRUE) ||
    grepl("current service outage", instructions, fixed = TRUE)
  compromise_rule <- grepl("compromised account", instructions, fixed = TRUE)
  outage <- grepl(
    "outage|unavailable|blocking|stopping|down",
    ticket,
    ignore.case = TRUE
  )
  compromised <- grepl(
    "unknown user|stranger gained access|attacker|unknown login|compromised",
    ticket,
    ignore.case = TRUE
  )

  urgent <- (outage_rule && outage) || (compromise_rule && compromised)
  list(severity = if (urgent) "urgent" else "routine")
})

reflection_fixture <- new_fixture_chat(
  "fixture-reflection",
  function(prompt, type, ...) {
    account_failure <- grepl(
      "Expected urgent but got routine",
      prompt,
      fixed = TRUE
    ) && grepl(
      "An unknown user took over my account.",
      prompt,
      fixed = TRUE
    )
    instructions <- if (account_failure) {
      complete_rule
    } else {
      partial_rule
    }
    list(instructions = instructions)
  }
)

task_chat <- task_fixture$chat
reflection_chat <- reflection_fixture$chat
old_cache <- configure_cache(enable = FALSE)
```

## 2. Write a feedback metric and score the baseline

What makes GEPA different from plain grid search is *why* it knows how to
improve a prompt. Wrapping a metric in `metric_with_feedback()` lets each row
return both a numeric `score` and a short `feedback` sentence explaining what
went wrong:

```{r feedback-and-baseline}
feedback_metric <- metric_with_feedback(
  function(prediction, expected) {
    correct <- identical(prediction$severity, expected$severity)
    list(
      score = as.numeric(correct),
      feedback = if (correct) {
        "Correct."
      } else {
        paste0(
          "Expected ", expected$severity, " but got ",
          prediction$severity,
          ". Check for an outage or a compromised account."
        )
      }
    )
  },
  field = "severity"
)

baseline_val <- evaluate(
  program,
  validation,
  metric = feedback_metric,
  .llm = task_chat,
  .cache = FALSE,
  .progress = FALSE
)

baseline_val$mean_score

data.frame(
  ticket = validation$ticket,
  expected = validation$severity,
  predicted = vapply(baseline_val$predictions, `[[`, character(1), "severity"),
  score = baseline_val$scores
)
```

With the vague baseline instruction (`"Use a quick baseline rule."`), the
module marks every ticket `routine` and misses both urgent cases (`1/3`).

## 3. Run a bounded GEPA search

Pass the task Chat as `.llm`, the reflection Chat as `.reflection_llm`, and a
resource cap through `optimizer_control()`:

```{r compile-gepa}
task_prompt_start <- length(task_fixture$audit$prompts)
reflection_prompt_start <- length(reflection_fixture$audit$prompts)

optimized <- compile(
  program,
  GEPA(
    metric = feedback_metric,
    population_size = 2L,
    generations = 2L,
    mutation_rate = 1,
    crossover_rate = 0,
    selection = "current_best",
    seed = 42L,
    verbose = FALSE
  ),
  train,
  valset = validation,
  .llm = task_chat,
  .reflection_llm = reflection_chat,
  control = optimizer_control(
    max_metric_calls = 40L,
    progress = FALSE
  )
)

result <- optimization_result(optimized)
result
```

## 4. Watch the instructions evolve

Inspecting `result$extensions$gepa` shows the exact lineage of candidates and
how each generation's wording improved on the validation set:

```{r candidate-lineage}
gepa_details <- result$extensions$gepa
candidate_ids <- names(gepa_details$candidates)

data.frame(
  candidate = candidate_ids,
  parent = vapply(candidate_ids, function(id) {
    parents <- gepa_details$parents[[id]]
    if (length(parents) == 0L) "seed" else paste(parents, collapse = ", ")
  }, character(1)),
  val_score = round(unname(gepa_details$val_aggregate_scores[candidate_ids]), 3),
  selected = candidate_ids == result$lineage$best_candidate_id,
  instructions = vapply(candidate_ids, function(id) {
    gepa_details$candidates[[id]]$component_values[[1L]]$value
  }, character(1)),
  row.names = NULL
)
```

Look at the three-step progression:

1. **Seed (`val_score = 0.333`):** `"Use a quick baseline rule."` misses both
   outages and compromised accounts.
2. **First rewrite (`val_score = 0.667`):** catches outages, but still misses
   `"An unknown user took over my account."` on the training set.
3. **Feedback-driven rewrite (`val_score = 1.000`):** GEPA feeds the missed
   training row and its feedback sentence back into the reflection prompt:

```{r reflection-feedback}
reflection_prompts <- reflection_fixture$audit$prompts[
  seq.int(reflection_prompt_start + 1L, length(reflection_fixture$audit$prompts))
]
feedback_prompts <- reflection_prompts[
  grepl("Feedback:", reflection_prompts, fixed = TRUE)
]
feedback_lines <- strsplit(feedback_prompts[[1L]], "\n", fixed = TRUE)[[1L]]
cat(grep("Feedback:", feedback_lines, value = TRUE), sep = "\n")
```

Seeing that specific miss, the reflection model adds `"or compromised account"`
to the instructions, and the new candidate scores `1.0` on validation.

```{r verify-invariants}
#| include: false
optimizer_task_prompts <- task_fixture$audit$prompts[
  seq.int(task_prompt_start + 1L, length(task_fixture$audit$prompts))
]
optimizer_prompts <- paste(c(optimizer_task_prompts, reflection_prompts), collapse = "\n")
stopifnot(
  isTRUE(all.equal(as.numeric(baseline_val$mean_score), 1 / 3)),
  length(feedback_prompts) > 0L,
  grepl("Expected urgent but got routine", feedback_prompts[[1L]], fixed = TRUE),
  grepl(train$ticket[[3L]], feedback_prompts[[1L]], fixed = TRUE),
  !any(vapply(holdout$ticket, grepl, logical(1), x = optimizer_prompts, fixed = TRUE)),
  isTRUE(result$best_score == 1),
  isTRUE(result$budget$metric_calls == 28),
  isTRUE(result$budget$metric_calls <= result$budget$limits$max_metric_calls)
)
```

## 5. Check once on holdout

Now evaluate both the original and compiled modules on the untouched `holdout`
rows:

```{r heldout-comparison}
holdout_before <- evaluate(
  program,
  holdout,
  metric = feedback_metric,
  .llm = task_chat,
  .cache = FALSE,
  .progress = FALSE
)
holdout_after <- evaluate(
  optimized,
  holdout,
  metric = feedback_metric,
  .llm = task_chat,
  .cache = FALSE,
  .progress = FALSE
)

data.frame(
  ticket = holdout$ticket,
  expected = holdout$severity,
  before = vapply(holdout_before$predictions, `[[`, character(1), "severity"),
  after = vapply(holdout_after$predictions, `[[`, character(1), "severity")
)

c(before = holdout_before$mean_score, after = holdout_after$mean_score)
```

```{r verify-holdout}
#| include: false
stopifnot(
  isTRUE(holdout_before$mean_score == 0.5),
  isTRUE(holdout_after$mean_score == 1)
)
```

## 6. Read the budget and choose objectives

`optimization_result(optimized)$budget` tracks every metric call spent inside
`compile()`. Baseline and final holdout evaluations sit outside that budget:

```{r budget-summary}
gepa_budget <- result$budget
data.frame(
  phase = c(
    "GEPA compile",
    "Baseline validation",
    "Before and after holdout",
    "Total across this walkthrough"
  ),
  metric_calls = c(
    gepa_budget$metric_calls,
    nrow(validation),
    2L * nrow(holdout),
    gepa_budget$metric_calls + nrow(validation) + 2L * nrow(holdout)
  )
)
```

With one metric, GEPA ranks candidates by that score. When you supply several
named objectives via `metrics = list(...)` and keep the default
`selection = "pareto"`, GEPA retains the non-dominated Pareto front instead of
collapsing trade-offs into a single weighted sum (`selection = "current_best"`
ranks by the first metric alone).

## 7. Run GEPA on live models

On real data, pair a fast task model with a strong reflection model and set a
cost/call budget (if you omit `.reflection_llm`, GEPA uses `.llm` for
reflection as well). Finite limits are checked between rows and provider calls,
so treat `max_cost` as a soft budget rather than a hard billing ceiling:

```{r live-gepa}
#| eval: false
live_optimized <- compile(
  program,
  GEPA(
    metric = feedback_metric,
    population_size = 6L,
    generations = 3L,
    seed = 42L
  ),
  train,
  valset = validation,
  .llm = ellmer::chat_openai(model = "gpt-6-luna"),
  .reflection_llm = ellmer::chat_openai(model = "gpt-6-astra"),
  control = optimizer_control(
    max_metric_calls = 80L,
    max_provider_calls = 50L,
    max_cost = 1,
    checkpoint_path = file.path(tempdir(), "gepa-checkpoint.rds")
  )
)

optimization_result(live_optimized)
```

GEPA supports checkpoint resume for sequential `round_robin` searches over
plain prediction modules and built-in pipelines; see
[GEPA](../reference/GEPA.html) for the full checkpoint contract, and
[dsprrr for DSPy users](dspy-comparison.html) for how dsprrr's `GEPA()` compares
with DSPy 3.5.0.

## Where GEPA fits

- **GEPA** evolves instructions from failures and textual feedback.
- **[Flex](flex-optimization.html)** lets GEPA rewrite a whole program's
  structure, not only its instructions.
- **[Omni](omni-meta-optimization.html)** compares several optimizers from one
  starting point and continues from the best.
- **[Agentic optimization harnesses](agentic-optimization-harnesses.html)** let
  an outer research agent explore hypotheses and propose multi-module edits.
